title: Velma Middleton and eating on the road
summary: He remembers Velma's rapport with Louis and the junk food and fruit musicians ate between jobs.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Velma was so great, she was a great personality herself. Velma and Louie had a rapport that

was out of this world. Velma on the records they did "That's My Desire." They sang a lot of blues together. That's Velma. I remember Velma when we played, it was in Florida, she'd get a whole bag of grapefruit, she'd be reaching up there, had it on top of the seat, she'd peel that thing and just ate it up, gobbled it up -- she liked a lot of fruit. I like a lot of fruit myself. I used to -- that's part of the role, you have so much time to go so many miles to go to a performance and you don't have time to eat, so what you do, you go outside before you take the run to the place where you're going to work. If you don't have time to eat, you go into the store and get some crackers or some sardines or fruit, mostly fruit, this is when you're on the road. All the road people did that, travelers did.
When you'd eat like that you'd drink juices sometimes or mostly milk and sometimes I guess beer.
Right right. Soda, get some soda.
You ate what you'd call junk food now. Junk food was great to have because you didn't have time to eat a decent meal until after you performed. Invariably most times you have to go a long

I'm sure, though, that some of the musicians didn't -- it didn't suit them very well when they ate like that, some of them I guess probably got sick sometimes after a while or -- I don't know.
When you're on the road you've got a pretty strong stomach and you have to have a strong bladder. If you drink too much you have to stop the bus or car inspection, they called it.
And look at the tires while -- you know what's happening.
If anybody wanted to go out to, you know, "Stop the bus." "I want to inspect the tires."
